source.title: Effective dimension of machine learning models
source.authors: Amira Abbas; David Sutter; A. Figalli; S. Woerner

record.tranche_reason: The study varies the proportion of randomized training labels and measures test error, using a different experimental setup to examine generalization under label randomization.
record.gate_note: The randomized-label experiments report test-error curves, but the text does not give exact test-error values or state that test performance reaches chance. Model-size experiments concern V2's width trend, but do not state that the tested models reach zero training error at each size, so they are not cataloged as V2 results. Effective-dimension measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own width-versus-test-error and randomized-label experiments in two-hidden-layer leaky-ReLU networks. Section 5 explicitly describes the width experiments as training to zero error, so they bear on V2 despite Appendix C.1 specifying a 200-epoch budget. The randomized-label experiments bear on V1 but do not establish its full conjunction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present local effective dimension as a promising capacity measure that correlates with generalization error in their experiments and admits a theoretical generalization bound; they call for further investigation of bound tightness and broader empirical settings.
record.recipe_differences: Two-hidden-layer fully connected leaky-ReLU networks trained with batched SGD; randomization begins at 20%, and the study measures effective dimension alongside test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and randomized-label proportion vary; the study reports separate MNIST and CIFAR10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized local effective dimension decreases alongside test error with increasing model size and increases alongside test error with increasing label randomization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Fisher-information-based local effective dimension correlates with test error in these fully connected network experiments.

record.problems: The randomized-label findings are shown in figures without exact per-condition test-error values in the text; results are averages over 10 trials and some runs may terminate before fitting to zero training error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Model-size results in Figures 1a and 2a were not included because the text does not state zero training error for every size, as V2 requires.

untested.parts: Achieved near-perfect fitting at full label randomization and chance-level held-out accuracy are not established. Natural-label generalization is measured separately in the model-size experiments, contrary to the record's blanket statement that no natural-label comparison exists.

The interpolation threshold and behavior near it are not measured. The exact original one-hidden-layer ReLU, convergence-based recipe is not replicated; these experiments use two hidden layers, leaky ReLU, and 200 epochs.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measurement or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Add MNIST width-versus-test-error results. Although rows_left_out declares their exclusion, its rationale overlooks Section 5's explicit zero-training-error description. Preserve the qualification that Appendix C.1 reports 200 epochs without per-size training errors.
missing.versions: V2; natural-label performance component of V1

missing.what: Add CIFAR10 width-versus-test-error results. Although rows_left_out declares their exclusion, its rationale overlooks Section 5's explicit zero-training-error description. Preserve the qualification that Appendix C.1 reports 200 epochs without per-size training errors.
missing.versions: V2; natural-label performance component of V1

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is justified by R1–R10: worsening performance with increasing corruption establishes neither the complete claim nor its failure. The supplied figure text contains axis labels but does not reliably expose individual plotted values. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a natural-label (0% randomization) comparison, random-label training accuracy, or whether test accuracy at 100% randomization is at chance. It uses fully connected networks, not the listed Inception, AlexNet, and MLP settings.

relationships.condition: MNIST; two-hidden-layer leaky-ReLU networks widened from approximately 20,000 to 100,000 parameters.
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than extracted rows: Section 5 describes zero-training-error models whose test error declines with increasing width; Appendix C.1 specifies 200 epochs but supplies no per-size training errors.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decrease in test error among wider, perfectly fitting MNIST networks remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR10; two-hidden-layer leaky-ReLU networks widened from approximately 500,000 to 10,000,000 parameters.
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than extracted rows: Section 5 and Figure 2a describe declining test error as zero-training-error models grow; Appendix C.1 specifies 200 epochs but supplies no per-size training errors.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decrease in test error among wider, perfectly fitting CIFAR10 networks remains unverified.
